title: Effect of increasing dietary folate on red-cell folate: implications for prevention of neural tube defects
authors: Cuskelly GJ, McNulty H, Scott JM
population: Women among university staff and students in Northern Ireland, randomised to 400 µg/day folic acid supplement, an extra 400 µg/day from folic acid-fortified foods, an extra 400 µg/day of food folate, dietary advice, or control; 41 completed
funder: not stated in the abstract; full text not accessible
result: Results read from the published abstract. Red cell folate rose significantly over 3 months only with the folic acid supplement or fortified foods (P < 0.01 for both). Extra food folate and dietary advice raised food folate intake (P < 0.001 and P < 0.05) without a significant change in red cell folate. The authors judged advice to rely on folate-rich foods to optimise folate status misleading.
